drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 56-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.9, creatinine 1.01, hemoglobin 13.3, platelets 235, sodium 141, wbc 6.1; vitals dbp 75-80, heart_rate 76-81, map 94-99, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 131-137, spo2 97-98, temp 37-37.2
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.02, hemoglobin 13.3, platelets 241, sodium 141, wbc 6.5; vitals dbp 76-80, heart_rate 77-81, map 94-98, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 131-138, spo2 97-98, temp 37-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 56-year-old male, length of stay 2 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
